items.title: Review and merge PR #133
items.body:
One speed change: the game’s and the lobby’s canvases draw one frame at a time on the GPU. Also four fixes found in review, four silent fallbacks made visible, seven checks or rules now enforced, two phone and screen-reader fixes, security headers, and the bench made to time what the player sees. CI was green on cf92a12 (client, server-tests, all three e2e shards; Cloudflare preview deployed), which carries every app commit of the branch.

It breaks CLAUDE.md’s “one PR per session, scoped to one logical change”: the run’s instructions asked for one branch and one PR, and it mixes the pacer with bench, lint, CI and small client fixes, as the last run did.

items.recommend: Split it as you did last time: the pacer and its two review fixes (a7cf4a4, f8ab886) as one PR; the bench changes (d95a58b, 41e1557, 74c93b9, 0f99624, 4b93f7d’s bench part, d5ed032); the checks and lint (2286468, 6f8dffe, 37d4cc9); the small client fixes (7eed7fb, 14d81fe, 9134a11, 9e5ca37). Or squash-merge it as is.

items.title: The pacer breaks the speed rule on one primary row: keep it, and time that row to the picture?
items.body: The run’s rule is no scenario slower than main beyond noise, never more than 3%. The primary row “A move landing, the player’s” is 17% slower on the final commit, every pair (1.16 1.09 1.31 1.14; the A/A on identical code gave +0.6%). I kept the pacer anyway, and this is yours to overrule. The primary rows “A move landing” and “Selecting a piece” stop when render() returns, the moment the frame is handed to the GPU. In software rendering the GPU then draws it for a long time. On main, the frame showing a move was drawn 2.3–2.4 s after the move, while the row said 163–176 ms. The pacer hands a frame over only once the previous one is drawn, so the hand-over row reads later (the player’s move +17%, not called) while the picture comes 5× sooner. This run added the GPU-drawn rows beside the old ones; bench/primary.mjs still names the old ones.

items.title: The lobby and the entrance on a slow GPU: fewer pictures, on time
items.body: Before, a GPU that drew three pictures a second also slowed the motion: each picture stepped the lobby’s clock by at most a quarter second, so the beats ran slow. Paced, the motion keeps its own time and the GPU draws what it can. The way into a game against the computer now ends after 8.8 s instead of 15.4 s, and joining a game shows the board after 1.6 s instead of 5.5 s. A real GPU that keeps up draws every frame as before. Recordings (the showcase’s stepped clock) draw every frame and match main frame for frame (top and bottom rows below; the middle row is the first version, before that rule).

figure.caption: Showcase --lobby, the handover at 9.0, 9.2, 9.4, 9.6 s. Top: main. Middle: paced, before the stepped-clock rule (a dark frame at 9.4 s). Bottom: kept version.

rows.only: (Game setup · (join: click → joiner’s first frame|joiner: long tasks total|create: click → share link)|Playing the computer · way in)

charts.caption: The way in, final A/B against main, 4 pairs.

items.recommend: Keep it. It changes how CLAUDE.md’s lobby rule plays out: the rule caps each step at LOBBY_MAX_STEP so a slow renderer still plays each beat in about its own time; paced, the beats keep their time more closely, with fewer pictures, and e2e’s waitForBoard (which waits on the whole handover) passes in CI. The look in real time on a slow GPU is not checked (recordings draw every frame), and two reviewer items stay open: DOM fades leading the paced picture (RV9) and the “useFrame ran, so it was drawn” audit (RV6). Try the preview build on your phone (improve-20261014-0357.3d-chess.pages.dev) and judge the arrival and the handover by eye: that is the one thing the bench cannot see.

  • The computer’s search speed +29% in the final A/B (1.57 1.06 1.12 1.48), on code the branch does not touch. Re-run with 6 pairs after grading: +5.5%, pairs both ways (0.89 1.00 1.08 0.92 1.46 1.06), not called. Its median is above the 3% cap, but it is within noise: the pairs disagree on the direction, and the code it runs (src/ai/) is not changed by the branch.

items.title: Calls the reviewers raised that are yours
items.body:
• Anyone with a game’s link can take either seat (ARCHITECTURE.md lists it as a non-goal). A per-seat secret would close it.
  • The socket accepts any Origin; the logs pair game ids with IPs.
  • Copy: the “seat moved” notice explains its own button; the move box’s hint repeats its label; “tap a ring” shows to mouse players.
  • viewport-fit=cover (I3′) also needs the HUD’s left and bottom edges inset.

items.title: The noise band: identical code against itself
items.body: The run began with an A/A (4 pairs). It called the opponent’s move −49% on identical code: the frame with the move waits 14–290 ms behind frames the GPU already has queued, and the queue lined up differently on each side. That queue is what the pacer removes.

items.title: The game’s and the lobby’s canvases draw one frame at a time on the GPU (a7cf4a4, f8ab886)
items.body: Each canvas draws its own frames. If the GPU has not finished the previous one (a fence), the next is skipped and asked for again; the motion still steps every display frame. A lost context, a fence that never passes (60 frames at most) and the warm-up’s one frame are handled; each has a test that fails without it. 70 lines of app code (the pacer).

items.title: The bench times what the player sees (74c93b9, 0f99624, d5ed032, d95a58b, 41e1557)
items.body:
• Each frame now records when the GPU finished it; the move and selection sections report those times beside the hand-over times.
  • The orbit helper turned until its time was up, so the angle depended on the frame rate; it now turns exactly its angle.
  • The A/B verdict dropped a pair at 0 from its agreement check, so it could call a row against one pair’s direction; the rule is now in bench/verdict.mjs with a test.
  • run.mjs ran something else on a typo’d flag or tier, overwrote RESULTS.md and exited 0; it now refuses (exit 2).
  • The computer section records blank cells no more: it fails when no worker started or a move had no search.

items.title: Silent fallbacks now say so (7eed7fb, 4b93f7d)
items.body:
• The computer’s search answering “no move” where the rules have one now logs, as a refused move already did.
  • A stored computer game that cannot be read (the only copy) now says why in the console.
  • linkAhead reports how it ended, and the select section shows it beside the first pick.

items.title: Checks that could pass on broken code, and rules nothing enforced (2286468, 6f8dffe, 37d4cc9)
items.body:
• The computer e2e tests passed with the search broken; they now fail on any fallback, page error or frame sent to the server (a planted broken search fails them).
  • The chunk-failure test passed before the chunk was even asked for; it now waits for the failure.
  • Lint now catches globalThis./self. timers, requestIdleCallback, new Date(), any mention of __r3fState outside the game canvas, and pointer handlers in three/scene (six planted escapes fail).
  • CI’s uv sync --locked fails a lock that no longer matches pyproject (checked on a copy).

items.title: Phone, screen reader and headers (14d81fe, 9134a11, 9e5ca37)
items.body:
• Upright on a phone, the open move list covers the tower’s lower levels; a press elsewhere or Escape now closes it, as the game menu does.
  • The tutorial’s words are a live region, so a screen reader hears each step while focus stays on Next.
  • public/_headers: no framing by other sites, nosniff, a referrer that names only the site.

choices.intro:
• Kept the pacer although the primary hand-over row for the player’s move leaned +17% (the GPU-drawn row is −81%, called); the row’s definition is put to you above.
  • Left bench/primary.mjs unchanged.
  • A frame waits for the GPU at most 60 display frames (about a second at 60 Hz).
  • Under a stepped clock (window.__vclock: the showcase, orbit.spec) the pacer draws every frame.
  • The bench’s orbit now turns an exact angle; its “after a turn” rows are not comparable with earlier runs.
  • Added _headers (no framing, nosniff, referrer) and uv sync --locked.
  • On a phone the open move list closes on a press elsewhere or Escape.
  • The computer’s fallbacks log with console.error, an unreadable stored game with console.warn.
  • Skipped lenses 1 and 10 (no dependency changed since they last ran).

notConfirmed.intro:
• The headers on Cloudflare Pages: the sandbox’s proxy refuses pages.dev, so I could not fetch the preview.
  • The pacer on a real phone GPU and on Safari (WebGL2 fences): the bench is software rendering only. The 60-frame cap bounds a fence that never passes.
  • Whether the DOM fades of the handover (the lobby canvas’s opacity, the entrance’s scene opacity) visibly lead the picture on a slow real GPU (reviewer’s RV9).
  • A full local e2e run of the final commit: the full suite ran locally on the pacer’s first commit (38 passed; the one failure was a font the scratch worktree could not serve, passing from the real worktree) and in CI on cf92a12.
  • The start page’s first click (+22% in the final A/B): not re-run with more pairs (the search speed was: +5.5%, not called).

merge.intro: No other sessions were active, and main did not move during the run. ARCHITECTURE.md now describes the pacer and the headers; CLAUDE.md is unchanged. Proposed, not made: in CLAUDE.md’s “Performance”, a line saying the move and selection rows time the hand-over and the “drawn by the GPU” rows time the picture.
